issues.description: The solution repository uses a different method name for the Developer course participation method than the problem statement and template. The problem statement and template expect an instance method attend(course:), but the solution implementation declares participateIn(course:) while the solution's Client still calls attend(course:). This name mismatch is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation/runtime confusion and prevents the solution code from matching the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name and signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution implementation participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) and update any internal references, or (B) change the template/problem and Client to use participateIn(course:). The preferred fix is to rename the method in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift (solution) to func attend(course: Course?) { ... } so it matches the problem statement, the template stub, and the Client call.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define and expect a Developer method named attend(course:), but the solution implementation uses a differently named method participateIn(course:). This divergent identifier for the same conceptual operation (a developer attending a course) creates a direct mapping confusion for students and also leads to an internal mismatch in the solution (Client calls attend(...) while Developer defines participateIn(...)).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across all artifacts. Rename the solution's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) (or update the problem/template to use participateIn) so the method name matches the problem statement and the template. Also ensure Client calls the same method name. This preserves the intended learning mapping and removes the compile/runtime mismatch.
